scope: Native private credential sync, scoped snapshots, signaling and ICE metadata; no native private payload transport or URM2 rollout

verification.model_vector_note: One old Python enum-error expectation includes the existing Go trickle-candidate extension
verification.user_service_test_executable: Previously built CLI-publication release; production checks execute the newly packaged public agent

checks: ClientSync message normalization and nested validation match retained fixtures with the current candidate enum extension
ICE configuration and relay routes are bounded; peer-scoped TURN REST credentials match an independent HMAC-SHA1 fixture
Only active private credentials and authorized machine/workspace ownership permit sync
Snapshots include only incident grants and reachable peers without public/private credentials or unrelated peer identities
UTC RFC3339 snapshot expiry preserves the existing Go timestamp decoder contract
Sender fingerprints, candidate limits and negotiation direction are validated independently of candidate LAN addresses
Message retries deduplicate and acknowledgements cannot remove another recipient's messages
Both source and target restart contexts and certificate rotations invalidate stale signaling
Expired signaling is filtered without waiting for TTL deletion; disabled/deleting machines and revoked memberships are denied
Production ingress rejects public machine credentials at the private signaling endpoint and retains all previous production checks
limitations: Positive private sync tests use the native router with real isolated MongoDB; production private credential enrollment and a real private-client handshake remain unverified
Native private enrollment/bootstrap, hostname/group mutation and gateway relay remain incomplete
Native TUN/DNS/ICE/DTLS transport, certificate-possession proof, agent enforcement and background path selection remain incomplete
This does not prove private payload connectivity, shortest-path selection or physical throughput
Legacy service takeover, platform lifecycle, crash-safe updates and production adoption remain outstanding
No commit, push, URM2 deployment, registered-agent upgrade or final physical-machine benchmark performed
